Anyone using imgur for picture hosting? I'm not sure what the image storage cap is, but it's associated with Reddit's Image hosting somehow, so I'd think it would be here to stay.

Advertisement was how flickr and photobucket used to run their business model until they got bought out or leadership changed. That's when policies change. It's still unclear if these companies will survive charging a fee, but I think flickr has a better chance of survival than photobucket because they observed photobucket make many fatal mistakes before they came up with their own approach to charging people.

posts.body_html:
Something to keep in mind when using any free image hosting platform: If you aren’t paying for the product, then you are the product. Which means as soon as they can’t make money off of you and your content, then you aren’t needed anymore.

The only permanent solution is to pay for hosting your images on AWS/web hosting/somewhere.
